presentation.label: TRACK-KEYED COMPRESSION
presentation.summary: Drive the stock COMPRESSOR detector from any audio track, with a base-width key filter, key gain and audition.
presentation.overview: The stock COMPRESSOR gains MON, KEY, KGN, KBAS and KWID beside RMS on its SETUP page. Choose T1-T8 as the detector input, set its gain, isolate it with a high-pass (KBAS, in Hz) and a low-pass a set number of octaves above it (KWID), or audition it on the receiving track.
highlights: KEY selects OFF or any of T1-T8, including the other DSP core, on a rotary switch.
KBAS is the key's high-pass (18 dB/oct, OFF or 20 Hz-19.6 kHz); KWID its low-pass, 0.5-9.9 octaves above KBAS (12 dB/oct, or OFF). They cannot cross.
KGN sets the key's gain, about -24 to +24 dB around 64.
MON auditions the processed key on the receiving track; switching it, or changing KEY while it is on, crossfades instead of clicking.
Stock ATK, REL, THRS, RAT, GAIN, MIX and RMS remain available.
usage: Select COMPRESSOR in FUNC + FX1/FX2 SETUP with LEVEL and YES.
Hold FUNC and press the selected FX button to open SETUP; choose the key with encoder C.
To duck from a kick's fundamental, set KBAS to about 30-40 Hz and KWID to about 1.2-1.5 octaves.
Turn MON OFF before normal listening; KEY OFF restores self-keying.

access.location: Audio track FX1 or FX2: COMPRESSOR in FUNC + FX SETUP; main compression controls on page 1; RMS and MON/KEY/KGN/KBAS/KWID on page 2.
steps: Select the receiving audio track. Hold FUNC and press FX1 or FX2 to open its SETUP chooser.
Turn LEVEL to COMPRESSOR and press YES. The visible name stays COMPRESSOR; the module takes that stock row on FX1 and in the FX2 chooser.
Press the selected FX button for ATK, REL, THRS, RAT, GAIN and MIX. Hold FUNC and press that FX button for SETUP with RMS, MON, KEY, KGN, KBAS and KWID.
In SETUP use encoder B for MON, C for KEY, D for KGN, E for KBAS and F for KWID.
Set KEY to OFF and MON to OFF to restore self-keying; choose NONE to remove the effect.

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: Stock attack control, raw 0-127; determines how quickly compression engages. Exact time mapping is inherited from stock.

controls.name: REL
controls.doc: Stock release control, raw 0-127; determines recovery after detector level falls.

controls.name: THRS
controls.doc: Stock threshold, raw 0-127; lower it until the selected key causes gain reduction.

controls.name: RAT
controls.doc: Stock compression ratio, raw 0-127; raise it to increase compression.

controls.name: GAIN
controls.doc: Stock output make-up gain, raw 0-127. This is distinct from KGN, which changes the detector input.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Stock dry/wet balance, raw 0-127; 127 is fully processed and 0 is dry.

controls.name: RMS
controls.doc: Stock RMS detector control, raw 0-127; retained on page 2 without changing its implementation.

controls.name: MON
controls.doc: ON plays the processed key on this receiving track instead of its output, after both effects; OFF is normal compression. OFF on the left, ON on the right (stored 2 = OFF, 3 = ON); a COMPRESSOR saved with an earlier version comes up with MON OFF. Switching it crossfades over 256 samples.

controls.name: KEY
controls.doc: OFF restores self-keyed stock detection; T1-T8 selects that track, including tracks on the other DSP core. A rotary switch on the LCD that moves one position per detent, also with the encoder pressed. A KEY change made while MON is audible waits for MON to fade, then takes the new key.

controls.name: KGN
controls.doc: The key's gain before the detector, about -24 to +24 dB; 64 is unity. Smoothed at block rate. The LCD shows the stock bipolar offset, not dB.

controls.name: KBAS
controls.doc: The key's high-pass, 18 dB/oct Butterworth: 0 is OFF, 1-127 run from 20 Hz to 19.6 kHz on a 1/16-octave grid. The LCD shows Hz.

controls.name: KWID
controls.doc: The key's low-pass, 12 dB/oct Butterworth, set as a distance above KBAS: 0.5 to 9.9 octaves, 127 is OFF. With KBAS OFF it counts from 20 Hz. The LCD shows octaves; a link clip ties it to KBAS.

limitations: Replaces COMPRESSOR on FX1 and in the FX2 chooser with the same stock effect ID 0x18; the visible effect name remains COMPRESSOR.

With Keep stock FX2 effects on, SPRING REV gives up its code space for this module; reassign any old SPRING REV slots. With it off, every stock FX2 effect leaves the FX2 chooser and the stock FX1 effects stay.

It builds beside every other visible module alone. Among the nine visible modules other than Analog BD, 648 of the 1,024 selections that contain it build (786 with 0.1.2): 0.2.0's two ColdFire units (1,216 B) leave less effect-menu and cave space, so 138 more selections are refused, the smallest Euclid with Scale Quantizer. The selection checker says which applies.
Beside Analog BD, 146 of the 212 Analog BD selections build (162 with 0.1.2); its larger DSP section (677 words a core) no longer fits core A in 16, the smallest Analog BD with Airwindows Chorus.
It cannot be combined with MIDI Scenes, which is standalone firmware.
Its core-private keybus and cross-core window overlap BusDelay and BusVerb, which Modwerk does not carry; the native resource ledger refuses them beside it.
A 0.1.x COMPRESSOR keeps its KEY; KGN takes the old KFLT, KBAS the old KGN, KWID the old MON, and MON comes up OFF.
Cross-core keys use a buffered shared window, two blocks late on the beta base whatever the cores' enable order; no exact hardware latency is claimed.
Every download carries the core logger; the module's LCD pages are identical with and without it.
The DSP figures are emulator measurements of whole core loops on a real project, not chip timing.
A COMPRESSOR saved with an earlier version (0.1.x, or 0.2.0 before 25 October 2026) comes up with MON OFF.

resources.recorded: 2026-10-24; emulator load measurement, static ColdFire bound and exact memory inventory

storage.label: Declared DSP reservation
storage.conditions: Full reservation of the module's own contribution including inherited stock state/scratch and complete hardware DSP stack capacity; no new heap, SDRAM or delay buffer. The key filters' state sits inside stock COMPRESSOR's instance block. Two ColdFire units (600 B + 616 B) and 612 DSP code words and 65 table words per core. See TESTING.md.

processing.label: Busiest core, eight keyed instances
processing.conditions: ot_emu load meter on the OT DEMO project: every FX1 and FX2 slot of one core holding a keyed COMPRESSOR (filters on, MON ON), the whole core loop in modelled cycles a sample, peak over 300 frames including the filters' glides and the MON fade; stock firmware with stock COMPRESSORs peaks at 1,298. Budget 4,535 a sample.

impact.conditions: Sixteen keyed compressors (eight per core); emulator figures, not chip timing.

cpu.rationale: sc_norm, a per-frame check of the sixteen FX slots: 144 instructions with no compressor, 752 when sixteen stale compressors reset in one frame (static frame bound 8,192 of a 9,577-cycle allowance). UI callbacks (formatters and the KEY switch) run at the 30 Hz redraw, at most 174 authored instructions each.

dsp.rationale: Key tap, detector with the base-width filters and MON crossfade. Eight keyed instances on a core peak at 1,743 modelled cycles a sample in the emulator against 4,535 (stock COMPRESSORs: 1,298).

memory.rationale: 26,288 bytes at sixteen instances including inherited stock buffers; no new heap/SDRAM delay storage.

tests.summary: Native octabam builds 0.2.0 alone and in 965 of the suites' selections (648 of 1,024 visible, 171 of 512 historical, 146 of 212 with Analog BD); both ColdFire units equal the author's references; the beta base's resident engine and controller pass the resident-engine, controller, registry and stock-free checks; emulator load of eight keyed instances a core; static ColdFire bound and exact memory inventory.
gates: Native octabam and browser composition compared on the module's coverage set, with and without stock FX2
Native suites regenerated: 512 selections of the original eight modules, 1,024 of the nine visible modules and 212 Analog BD selections
ColdFire units byte-identical to the author's references (sc_cf 600 B 4984aba2..., sc_ui 616 B 157f883f...)

Beta base: resident engine (key phase two blocks late on every enable order, MON ends with its COMPRESSOR, split and placed engines bit-exact), the scinit site and COMPRESSOR bridges, controller stock-free scans, power-up check for 0.2.0's page 2
Resource ledger: declared DSP ranges, source literals and stock shared-window tenants
Source-only reproducible package build in the pinned toolchain
Emulator load (eight keyed instances a core), static sc_norm bound, exact memory inventory

conditions.parameterExtremes: KEY on every compressor, keyed from the other core; KGN 64, KBAS 40, KWID 30 (both filters on) and MON ON; filters OFF and MON OFF measured for comparison.
conditions.parameterModulation: All parameters set at once at frame 3: the filters' glides (coefficients recomputed each block a position moves) and MON's 256-sample fade fall inside the measured window.
conditions.modeSwitching: MON switched on and KEY taken while the transport plays; scinit runs when the effect is assigned.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight COMPRESSORs on one core (FX1 and FX2 on four tracks), the OT DEMO project playing. The figure is the whole core loop (stock dispatcher, every effect, this module), so it is not summed with other modules.
conditions.inputConditions: Emulator (ot_emu, datasheet cycles, no memory stalls), not chip timing. worstCase: one keyed instance's added cost over a stock COMPRESSOR, its share of the always-on tap and MON commit included: (1,742.9 - 1,298.3) / 8 = 55.6 cycles a sample, x 16, rounded up. maxConfiguration: the eight-instance core loop's peak, 1,742.9 x 16, everything on the core included.

conditions.parameterExtremes: sc_norm: every FX slot holding COMPRESSOR (id 0x18) with KEY 0..8 (left alone, but a MON other than 2/3 set OFF) and KEY 9..255 (reset to MON OFF, KEY OFF, KGN 64, KBAS OFF, KWID OFF), in the Part working store and the live lane; the MON/KEY/KBAS/KWID formatters and the KEY switch through the stock widget, knob and sprintf.
conditions.parameterModulation: LFO, p-lock, scene and CC changes write the same page-2 bytes the stock editor writes; sc_norm reads them once per frame and never calls the kernel or UI. A KEY inside 0..8 is never rewritten, so modulation inside the control range costs only the compare path.
conditions.modeSwitching: Part change, Part reload, project load and transport start bring stored page-2 bytes into the working store or the lane; each copy is judged only against its own FX id. The worst frame is sixteen stale compressors reset at once (both copies of all eight tracks' FX1 and FX2), priced cold.
conditions.maxLoad: Sixteen COMPRESSOR slots (FX1 and FX2 on eight tracks), both detour sites (0x4000cae8 every frame; 0x40003d1c has no static caller and never ran in a 600-frame coverage run, priced as if it also ran every frame). Budget: 10% of a 362.8 us frame at 264 MHz (9,577 of 95,779 cycles), Modwerk's ColdFire allowance; the other 90% is reserved for stock frame work. UI formatters run in the UI task at the 30 Hz redraw, outside the frame path (TESTING.md).
conditions.inputConditions: Signal-independent: sc_norm reads only FX ids and page-2 bytes. Stock-saved compressors (slots 8..11 = 0x7f/0/0/0), in-range keys and arbitrary byte values were exercised in the emulator; the bound covers every branch.

regions.name: Inherited stock X instance block (the key filters at r7+$1c..$2d inside it)
Two KEY GAIN and key-filter tables
Two shared Y windows including seeds/counters
Inherited low X scratch on both cores
ColdFire authored code (sc_cf 698 B, sc_ui 616 B)
Additional ColdFire caller stack (sc_norm peak, frame)
Additional ColdFire UI stack (KEY switch through its formatter)
Additional ColdFire UI stack (MON and KEY step handlers: two arguments and a return address)

memory.conditions: Full reservation of the module's own contribution including inherited stock state/scratch and complete hardware DSP stack capacity; no new heap, SDRAM or delay buffer. Measured on Modwerk's native image of this source (MAIN OS 131142e1...); see TESTING.md.

hardware.summary: The author flashed Modwerk's native image of this source, the module alone (MW_SC021), on an Octatrack MKI and reported it working: KBAS and KWID across their range with MON on and off, MON's OFF/ON switch and its OFF on older projects, KEY's pressed turn, the MON and KEY fades, and a MON ON project across a power cycle.
limitations: A functional report: duration, project, material and tempo were not reported, and the checklist was confirmed as a whole.
No measured chip timing, memory canary, recording, recovery or stress test; cross-core key latency was not measured.
The flashed image is the module alone; the Modwerk download (with the core logger), the USB beta base and selections with other modules were not flashed.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: duck T5 from a T1 kick
steps: Back up the project, work on a disposable copy, and put a kick on T1 and a sustained sample or loop on T5.
Select T5, hold FUNC and press FX1, turn LEVEL to COMPRESSOR and press YES. Press FX1 for the main page; hold FUNC and press FX1 to return to SETUP with the key controls.

Set KEY to T1 and leave KGN at 64, KBAS and KWID OFF and MON OFF. On the main page, keep MIX at 127, raise RAT and lower THRS until T5 dips when the T1 kick plays; adjust ATK and REL for the envelope you want.
To duck from the kick's fundamental only, set KBAS to about 30-40 Hz and KWID to about 1.2-1.5 octaves. Set MON to ON to hear what the detector hears, then back to OFF.
Return KEY to OFF and MON to OFF to restore self-keyed stock compression, or select NONE to remove the effect.
